Subject: Next steps — Migration & deployment mode selection (Hosted vs Dedicated vs Private)

Hi Samantha —

Thanks again for the call this morning. Quick recap and proposed next steps so we stay aligned: 

Recap (what you shared)
- Current stack: prototype running on a mix of self-hosted GPU instances + calls to GenericLLM API for embeddings.
- Key drivers: predictable latency for end-user features, stricter data residency for PHI-related workflows, and wanting to reduce per-query unit cost as volume ramps.
- Timeline: pilot in Q3, production decision by end of Q3.

Redwood deployment options we discussed
- Hosted API: fastest time-to-value, no infra ops; good for early pilot but may need add-on for data residency controls.
- Dedicated capacity: reserved GPU pools for predictable throughput and data isolation; fits teams that need SLA and lower tail latency with no infra ownership.
- Private (VPC / on-prem): full control and compliance for regulated data; longer lead time and higher setup effort.

Open questions / blockers for your team
1) Expected qps / peak concurrency for the pilot and production.
2) Any hard requirements on network isolation (e.g., must sit inside Lumina VPC) vs acceptable managed VPC peering.
3) Migration constraints: are there proprietary model variants or custom kernels you must keep, or are you open to using our curated open-model catalog and quantized variants?

Proposed next steps
- Rishi to share a brief technical note (attached) outlining Dedicated vs Private performance/cost tradeoffs for your typical inference patterns (token lengths, concurrency). — Action: Rishi (by Fri 16 Apr)
- Lumina to share expected qps and any compliance checklist items (SOC2 / PHI) that will affect architecture. — Action: Samantha (by Mon 19 Apr)
- Quick follow-up call next week to review migration checklist and decide whether we scope a Dedicated pilot or start with Hosted + data residency gating. I dropped three suggested times in the calendar invite.

Attachments: deployment-comparison-one-pager.pdf, lumina-migration-checklist.xlsx

Thanks —

Hi Samantha —

Short technical note on the two key asks you mentioned: running your custom model artifact and supporting a custom CUDA/kernel stack.

1) Dedicated capacity + custom artifacts
- We can support loading customer model artifacts into Dedicated pools. For models that are identical to open formats (e.g., PyTorch weights), we can host the exact artifact and run on our runtime variants that preserve numerical fidelity.
- If you require binary-identical execution using your custom CUDA kernels, the options are: (a) run in your Private deployment (VPC or on-prem) where you control the kernel stack; or (b) we can evaluate a Dedicated pool that we provision with the required kernel ABI, but that typically requires a partner-eng/dev cycle and a minimum commitment.

2) Hosted & fallback
- Hosted API cannot guarantee execution with your custom kernel stack. It is possible to serve a functionally identical model (same weights + Redwood-verified runtime) but not to run arbitrary customer kernels inside the hosted multi-tenant runtime.

3) Migration pattern recommendation
- Pilot path A (fast): Start with Hosted for non-PHI traffic and use a Dedicated pilot for PHI flows if you want Redwood-managed infra + lower latency. We can enable VPC peering and strict IAM to isolate traffic.
- Pilot path B (control): Use Private deployment for PHI from day one if kernel parity is required — Redwood will provide a private control plane and assist with on-prem packaging.

I've attached a short matrix (redwood-dedicated-pricing.pdf) with estimated cost deltas and lead times for provisioning Dedicated vs Private. Happy to run an infra sizing call if helpful.

Cheers,
Rishi Malhotra
Senior Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference

   - Stand up a small Dedicated pilot (1 GPU node equivalent) for PHI flows that need lower tail latency and stronger isolation. This node will host your exact model artifact; we'll evaluate kernel parity during the pilot.

2) Parallel work:
   - Dev + Lumina to run a quick kernel-parity test (Rishi + Dev) using a sandbox Dedicated instance. If kernel parity can't be achieved within the pilot window, we scope Private deployment for production.

3) Logistics / timeline:
